title: Comprehensive rotational study and astronomical search for cyclopropanecarboxaldehyde
question: Measure accurate rotational parameters and isomer stabilities of cyclopropanecarboxaldehyde (c-C3H5CHO) in the laboratory and search for its emission in Orion KL and Sgr B2(N).

what.value: Physical parameters and CH3CHO column densities of Orion KL components

evidence.quote: To model the CPCA emission in these components, we adopted physical parameters according to those derived by Cernicharo et al. (2016) and Tercero et al. (2018).

external_data.citation: Cernicharo et al. (2016); Tercero et al. (2018)

what.value: IRAM 30 m 3 mm survey data, physical parameters, and CH3CHO column density of Sgr B2(N)

evidence.quote: To estimate upper limits to the CPCA column density in the region, we adopted the physical parameters derived by Belloche et al. (2013) for CH 3 CHO (see Table 6).

what.value: Experimental dipole moments of trans and cis CPCA isomers

evidence.quote: The two CPCA isomers are near symmetric tops with moderate dipole moments that have been experimentally determined by Volltrauer & Schwendeman (1971).

recipe.goal: Perform quantum chemical calculations of CPCA isomers
recipe.method: Structural optimisation and harmonic/anharmonic vibrational frequency calculations using B3LYP, B97D, MP2, and CCSD with 6-311++G(d,p), cc-pVTZ, and aug-cc-pVTZ basis sets
key_parameters: MP2/6-311++G(d,p) level of theory for vibrational frequencies and vibration-rotation constants

recipe.goal: Measure and fit laboratory rotational spectra of cis and trans CPCA
recipe.method: Measure broadband rotational spectra in 31.5–50 GHz and 72–116.5 GHz with GACELA and fit rotational and centrifugal distortion constants using Watson's S-reduced Hamiltonian
key_parameters: Watson S-reduction in I^r representation (trans) and III^r representation (cis); frequency predictions up to 300 GHz; J_max = 90 for partition function
assumptions: T = 350 K for laboratory gas-phase relative stability; dipole moments from Volltrauer & Schwendeman (1971)

recipe.goal: Search for CPCA and derive column density upper limits in Orion KL and Sgr B2(N)
recipe.method: Generate LTE synthetic spectra with MADEX using fixed source physical parameters and compare to ALMA SV, IRAM 30 m, and GBT PRIMOS spectra to derive upper limits on column density
key_parameters: Orion KL: d_sou = 3 arcsec, T_rot = 150 K, v_LSR = 8.0 / 7.5 / 5.0 km s^-1, FWHM = 3.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 km s^-1; Sgr B2(N): d_sou = 3 arcsec, T_rot = 100 K, v_LSR = 63 / 73 km s^-1, FWHM = 8.0 km s^-1
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), uniform disc-type source model for beam dilution correction

evidence.quote: Assuming a temperature for our experiment of 350K, this implies an energy difference between both isomers of 44.05(75) cm −1 , with the trans species being the most stable.

score_reason: Laboratory line lists, spectroscopic constants, partition functions, and frequency predictions are publicly archived at CDS, and the ALMA SV and GBT PRIMOS datasets are public with clear LTE model parameters in Table 6, though ALMA cube imaging details are deferred to earlier papers and upper limits rely on visual comparison in MADEX.
rediscovery_reason: The CDS line lists and public ALMA SV / PRIMOS / IRAM 30 m datasets allow straightforward reproduction of the Hamiltonian fits (using SPFIT/ASFIT) and LTE column density upper limits.
